gaps.note: Starting from (eta, zeta): D becomes zeta+eta, the swap gives H = zeta+eta and D = eta, and D <- D - H then gives eta-(zeta+eta) = -zeta. So the recipe ends at (eta+zeta, -zeta), not (eta+zeta, zeta) as claimed. The last update must be D_tau <- H_sigma - D_tau (paper line 1420, 'D_j <- H_i - D_j'), which gives zeta.

gaps.quote: So the shear needs $2\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ interchanges plus $O(V)$ further work.
gaps.note: Inconsistent with the page, which says each update uses one interchange and Pi has rank_Q M ones, so the count is rank_Q M interchanges. The paper (Lemma matrix-shear, lines 1394-1411 and 1424-1442) states exactly a = rank interchanges, one per 1 of Pi. The factor 2 is wrong, and it also conflicts with the later claim that interchanges per wire are fewer than R.

gaps.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
gaps.note: Does not follow from 'q must not divide xi', which only constrains denominators. The paper (lines 1411-1415) chooses q to avoid every denominator in the finite table and every numerator of a diagonal entry of an invertible factor (e.g. q larger than all nonzero numerators and denominators), so the triangular factors stay invertible mod q^b. The page never states this reason or that the choice is made once for the finite table.

gaps.term: missing hypothesis: H before D on tape
gaps.quote: Each update $H_\sigma\leftarrow H_\sigma+D_\tau$ takes one interchange of two equal fields and two additions
gaps.note: The O(V) cost of the two additions, and the lower-triangular passes, rely on updating a later field from earlier ones in tape order. The paper's Lemma matrix-shear (line 1400) assumes every H_i comes before every D_j, so D_tau is a later field controlled by earlier H_sigma. The page never states this ordering hypothesis, so the reader cannot check that the two additions are linear-cost.

gaps.quote: $N$ the number of negative source projections
gaps.note: Neither explained nor linked. The reader of the linked network page has no notion of projections, edge matrices carrying subspaces, or negative sources. The paper (lines 1145-1170) defines them through subspace projections on the bit network's edges.

The reader is not told what matrix each edge carries or why its rank is a dimension change, so the formula, and what 'dimension lost on decreasing edges' means, cannot be checked. The page only attributes N>2L_b to the paper without stating why it holds (paper Proposition bit-motif-interface, lines 1138-1170).

gaps.quote: which the recurrence turns into a saving of a power of the chunk width (the chunk length)
gaps.note: No recurrence is stated or linked, and chunk width is not defined on this page. The reader cannot see how fewer than R interchanges per wire yields a power saving; the paper (lines 1320-1342) derives s_b/W_b < m^tau separately via recursive analysis.
